note: Independent semantic rejudgment 2026-11-12 against Section 6.1's silent discard of both dynamic authorization request kinds from untrusted sources. UntrustedSourceDiscarded sends an otherwise valid signed/current Disconnect to a listener trusting a different address, then an empty allowlist: both receive no response and cause zero teardowns; a loopback-trusting listener accepts the same identity with Disconnect-ACK. The added explicit current-accountant seed makes the trusted counterpart reach the intended session rather than fail later identity matching. SourceFilterDiscardsWhenNoServerResolved independently sends correctly authenticated CoA with an empty allowlist and requires silence; SourceFilterAnswersAConfiguredClient repeats from the trusted source and requires an actual CoA-NAK response for unknown session, proving admission rather than universal discard. isAllowedSource precedes packet authentication/dispatch and is false for an empty set. A permissive empty/unlisted-source guard or blanket drop would break these opposite controls. No new proof execution is claimed.
